You are testing one step ("A2") of an in-flight Zimmermann PWA Kit build, branch `feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed`, repo at /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa. You find problems, you never fix them. Do NOT edit/write/delete any file in the repo — read-only only (Read, Grep, Bash for read-only greps/find; you may run `npx vitest run <specific file>` if genuinely needed to observe existing test output, but do not create new test files or modify any existing one).

## Background
Step A2 added a fourth `variation: 'recentlyViewed'` to the `ZimmProductCard` organism at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.tsx`. When this variation is active (`!config.showContent`), instead of rendering the usual `ZimmProductCardMedia` + `ZimmProductCardContent` pair, the component renders:
```
<MediaOnlyCardLink to={href} display="block">
  <VisuallyHidden>{name}</VisuallyHidden>
  <ZimmProductCardMedia primaryImage={{...primaryImage, alt: ''}} hoverImage={...} images={images} swapOnHover={...} showControls badge={resolvedBadge} />
</MediaOnlyCardLink>
```
where `MediaOnlyCardLink = chakra(RouteLink)` (a plain wrap of react-router-dom's `Link` with Chakra style-prop support — NOT Chakra's own themed `<Link>` component). This is a brand new whole-card interactive element (a real `<a>` wrapping an entire image) that did not exist before this step. The recipe file `zimmProductCard.css.ts` was deliberately NOT touched by this step (confirmed separately) — the plan's own reasoning is that this variation renders no `Card-content` block per Figma (Desktop node `40000307:12444`, Tablet `40000730:13363`, Mobile `40000538:25030`), so none of the recipe's existing hover-reveal machinery (built for the OTHER three variations' stretched-link-overlay pattern) is needed here.

## What I've already independently confirmed myself (do not re-verify these — they are settled, real, CONFIRMED findings, not claims to re-derive)
- Flipping `showBadge`/`showHoverImageSwap` to `true` for this variation makes the corresponding suppression tests fail for real (ran it).
- Removing the `alt: ''` override makes the exact-accessible-name test fail for real, with the actual jsdom-computed accessible name shown as "Natura Dress Zimmermann dress, front" (concatenated) instead of "Natura Dress" (ran it).
- A single Tab reaches the real `<a href="/product/1">` and the next Tab skips past the whole card (ran it) — exactly one focusable element inside this variation's card.
- react-router-dom v5.3.4's real installed `Link` (`node_modules/react-router-dom/cjs/react-router-dom.js`) natively bails out on modifier-clicks/non-primary-button clicks before calling `history.push` — confirmed by reading the actual shipped source, so no click-passthrough handler is needed for this variation.
- **A real, confirmed defect I already found (do not spend time re-finding it, just note it if relevant to your own findings, but your OWN job is the items below):** if a caller supplies MORE than one image to a `recentlyViewed` card (which is type-permitted — `images` is a base prop, not gated per variation — even though the plan says the one real caller, SFCC-83's rail, will always supply exactly one), `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s carousel prev/next `<button>` elements end up nested INSIDE the new `<a>` (confirmed: `link.contains(nextButton) === true`), and clicking a "Next image" button ALSO fires the ancestor anchor's navigation (confirmed: a `<Route path="/product/1">` marker mounted after the click) — a real double-fire bug and invalid nested-interactive-HTML, currently unreachable only because the one specified caller (not yet built) is planned to always pass a single image.

## Your job — investigate these, independently, and report real findings

1. **Focus-ring reset check (the main thing I need from you).** `MediaOnlyCardLink` is a bare `chakra(RouteLink)` — it does NOT get Chakra's own `Link` theme recipe (that only applies if you use Chakra's actual `<Link>` component). It gets no custom `_focus`/`_focusVisible` styling of its own, and the recipe file wasn't touched. So this new whole-card anchor relies entirely on the BROWSER'S default focus outline for a real `<a>`. Search the codebase for anything that resets/removes default focus outlines globally or for anchors specifically — check `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts`, `overrides/app/theme/index.ts`, `overrides/app/theme/foundation/*`, any CSS reset, and Chakra's own default global styles (`theme.styles.global`) for anything like `outline: none`, `outline: 0`, a CSS reset library, or a `*:focus` rule. Also check whether this project's OTHER real anchors (e.g. the stretched-link overlay `<a>` inside `ZimmProductCardContent`'s `ProductNameLink`, or the footer's links) rely on an explicit `:focus-visible` recipe rule rather than the browser default — if EVERY other real link in this component family gets an explicit focus-ring token (`var(--zimm-focus-ring)` etc.) and this is the only one that doesn't, that's a real, concrete, reportable gap (a keyboard user tabbing to this new card-wide link might get no visible focus indicator at all, or an inconsistent one vs. every other card variation) — WCAG 2.4.7. Report exactly what you find, with file:line, and state plainly whether you found evidence of an actual missing focus indicator vs. just an absence of an EXPLICIT one (the implicit browser default might be entirely adequate — say which one it is, don't assume the worse case).
2. **Recipe state exhaustiveness for this new interactive element** (per the standing angle: "for every new interactive part in a recipe, cross-reference the Figma nodes named in the step against the pseudo-states defined in the recipe — `_hover`, `_focusVisible`, `_active`, `_disabled`. A designed state with no recipe entry is a real finding."). Does Figma (per the plan document's own citations — you don't have Figma access, so work from what `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-83+84/plan.md` says, search for "A2 —" and "recentlyViewed") describe ANY hover/focus/active visual treatment for this specific rail-tile card, distinct from the default state? Or does the plan's own evidence suggest the design has no distinct state here at all (in which case this angle is vacuous for this element, and you should say so plainly rather than invent a finding)?
3. **Hover-gating correctness** — is `MediaOnlyCardLink` itself a hover-gated reveal (a hidden-by-default part shown only on hover/focus)? Read the actual render code again: it isn't — it's a plain, always-visible link with no hidden state. Confirm this and state explicitly that this half of the angle is vacuous here (don't force a finding where there is a real absence of the pattern) — UNLESS you find something I've missed (e.g., does `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own carousel-arrow hover-reveal CSS from the shared recipe still apply to the arrows even inside this new branch, in a way that could interact badly with the new Link — you don't need to redo the double-fire proof, just note if the hover-reveal styling itself is a separate concern from the click bug).
4. **Cross-check the AC-4 accessibility narrative against SFCC-236's shared component's OWN test file precedent** — read `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx`'s own `ProductNameLink`/link implementation (grep for how IT achieves its accessible name and any focus styling it relies on) and compare: does `ProductNameLink` get an explicit focus style from `zimmProductCard.css.ts` or `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`, or does IT ALSO rely on the browser default? This tells us whether the new `MediaOnlyCardLink`'s reliance on the default (if that's what you find in #1) is a NEW gap this step introduced, or a pre-existing pattern this step is simply consistent with (in which case it's UNIFORM, not a defect unique to this step).

## Report format
Number your findings to match the 4 items above. Each: file:line, what you found, CONFIRMED (you read/ran something real) or PLAUSIBLE (reasoned), severity (🔴/🟡/🔵), UNIFORM or ONE-OFF. If an item turns out vacuous/clean, say so in one line, don't pad. End with what you could not verify (e.g., you have no way to render this in a real browser to see the ACTUAL visual focus ring — say so).

import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
import { CARD_SLOT, HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY, DESKTOP_QUERY } from '../../zimmProductCardShared';

/**
 * Same hover-capable-pointer gate `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts` already establishes for its own
 * arrows/indicator split — now a shared import from `zimmProductCardShared.ts` rather than each
 * file's own module-private copy, so the two can't silently drift. Governs the price <->
 * size-selector swap below, so both composed children's hover treatments engage together off the
 * exact same media feature, on this shared root.
 */

/**
 * A viewport-width gate, unrelated to `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` above — governs the PLP-only bag-icon
 * mobile hide (Fix D, SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit) below. Also a shared import from
 * `zimmProductCardShared.ts`, same reasoning as `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` above: this and
 * `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`'s own `root` padding step both need the identical `min-width`
 * gate, and a module-private copy in each file was exactly the drift risk this extraction removes.
 */

type ZimmProductCardStyleProps = {
  /** Home only — see VARIATION_CONFIG in index.tsx. Price is hidden at every breakpoint/pointer
   *  type by default and only appears once a hover-capable pointer actually hovers the card. */
  hoverRevealsPrice?: boolean;
  /** PLP + Wishlist — price is visible by default (Content's own natural rendering; no override
   *  needed for that half) and hides only once a hover-capable pointer hovers the card. */
  hoverHidesPrice?: boolean;
  /** PLP + Wishlist — the size-chip picker is hidden at every breakpoint/pointer type by default
   *  and only appears once a hover-capable pointer actually hovers the card, in the same
   *  media-query gate as the price swap above so both engage together. */
  hoverRevealsSizeSelector?: boolean;
  /** Fix C — true whenever ZimmProductCardContent actually mounted a notify-me button
   *  (`isUnavailable && onNotifyMe`, computed once in index.tsx as `showNotifyMe`). Unlike the two
   *  flags above, the "hidden by default" half lives INSIDE `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`, not outside it
   *  — see docblock point 4: a touch pointer must see notify-me unconditionally (confirmed via
   *  every Mobile Unavailable Figma reference), where price/the size-selector do the opposite. */
  hoverRevealsNotifyMe?: boolean;
  /** Fix C — true for a PLP/Wishlist card that would normally hover-swap to the size-selector
   *  (`config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector`) but is out of stock. Unlike every other flag here, this
   *  is not a pointer-type concern at all: the size-chip wrapper stays hidden permanently, in
   *  every state, on every device — see docblock point 4. */
  sizeSelectorUnavailable?: boolean;
  /** Fix D — PLP only (`VARIATION_CONFIG.plp.hideBagOnMobile` in index.tsx). A viewport-width
   *  concern, not a pointer-type one: hidden below `breakpoints.md`, visible from it up — see
   *  docblock point 5. */
  hideBagOnMobile?: boolean;
};

/**
 * Recipe for the product-card organism (ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard) — composes
 * ZimmProductCardMedia (Step 4) and ZimmProductCardContent (Step 5) with no styling of its own
 * for either child. This recipe's entire job is the cross-component concerns neither child can
 * own by itself:
 *
 *   1. THE STRETCHED-LINK OVERLAY. ZimmProductCardContent's `nameLink` renders the one real `<a>`
 *      in the whole composed tree. Its `::after` is stretched to `inset: 0` against THIS
 *      component's own `root` — the nearest positioned ancestor. Confirmed by reading
 *      `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts` directly: neither its `root` nor `nameRow`, `nameLink`, or
 *      any other part sets `position` anywhere in that file, so nothing between the `<a>` and
 *      this `root` intercepts the containing-block chain. (`ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `root`
 *      IS `position: relative`, but Media is a *sibling* of Content under this organism's root,
 *      never an ancestor of Content's `<a>`, so it has no bearing on this chain.)
 *   2. LIFTING EVERY OTHER INTERACTIVE CONTROL above that overlay — a z-index higher than the
 *      overlay's own (left unset), or the invisible overlay would intercept their clicks first.
 *      Four separate, single-selector keys rather than one comma-joined selector: verified via
 *      this project's own installed Stylis (v4.2.0 — the same engine Emotion/Chakra invoke at
 *      runtime, confirmed by direct compilation) that a comma-separated list DOES distribute this
 *      recipe's generated class across every branch correctly, but four plain keys need no such
 *      verification to trust at a glance and are each individually addressable from a test. Only
 *      ONE of the four (`content` buttons) also adds `position: relative` — that element is
 *      `position: static` by default in its own component recipe, so a positioned ancestor is
 *      needed for z-index to apply at all. `close`, `carousel`, and `media` are the three
 *      exceptions: `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own recipe already positions each of them directly
 *      (`close` via `position: absolute, top: 0, right: 0`; `carousel` via `position: absolute,
 *      top: 50%, ...`; `media` — its own root — via `position: relative`), so each needs (and
 *      gets) only the z-index bump here:
 *        - `close` — a competing `position` value previously declared alongside it had HIGHER
 *          specificity than Media's own rule (this rule is a class+attribute descendant selector;
 *          Media's is a single class) and silently won the cascade, knocking the remove button out
 *          of its pinned top-right corner into normal document flow (Fix 1). See the inline
 *          comment at that key below and index.test.tsx's "Fix 1" describe block for the proof.
 *        - `carousel` — Fix 3 (found during the manual real-browser check performed after the
 *          round-2 Scorer PASS, which explicitly flagged that check as still outstanding, not by
 *          any automated pass). The lift rule used to target
 *          `'[data-card-slot="carousel"] button'` — the two arrow BUTTONS individually, each given
 *          its own `position: relative, zIndex: 1` — identical in shape to the `content button`
 *          rule above, and every jsdom test passed. A real click in a real browser still landed on
 *          the overlay, not the arrow. Root cause: `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `carousel` part
 *          sets `transform: translateY(-50%)` (to vertically centre the arrow row against `slide`),
 *          and `transform` unconditionally creates a NEW stacking context on that element,
 *          regardless of its `position`/`z-index`. That traps each arrow button's `zIndex: 1`
 *          *inside* the carousel wrapper's own stacking context — it only wins ordering battles
 *          against the *other* arrow button, never against anything outside `carousel` (like the
 *          content overlay), because the whole `carousel` box is itself just an ordinary
 *          z-index:auto participant one level up — and, being earlier in DOM order than
 *          `[data-card-slot="content"]`, it lost. Moving the lift to the `carousel` WRAPPER itself
 *          (already `position: absolute` from Media's own recipe, so only `zIndex: 1` is needed
 *          here, same as `close`) fixes this: the wrapper's own stacking context — not one buried
 *          inside it — is what gets compared against the overlay, and it wins outright, carrying
 *          both arrow buttons above the overlay with it. This is exactly the gap
 *          index.test.tsx's own "KNOWN LIMITATION" docblock warns about — jsdom resolves no
 *          stacking contexts at all, so this shipped past every automated check and was only
 *          found by a real click in a real browser. See index.test.tsx's "Fix 3" describe block.
 *        - `media` — Fix I (SFCC-236, found via a real mobile-device touch-swipe check performed
 *          after this branch's own live testing round, not by any automated pass). The media/
 *          gallery scroll region itself was never added to this lift list, even though it is
 *          exactly as interactive as the controls nested inside it: with no z-index of its own,
 *          `[data-card-slot="media"]` sat at the same default/auto stacking layer the overlay
 *          itself occupies, so a touch swipe starting on the image landed on the invisible
 *          overlay `<a>` first and the real scroll container underneath never received the
 *          gesture — the slide indicator still rendered correctly (proving the image data/gallery
 *          logic was fine), but nothing paged. Missed earlier because `close`/`carousel`/content-
 *          buttons were each checked with a real CLICK (Fix 1, Fix 3 above) — and a click on the
 *          image happened to "work" by accident either way, since it also landed on the overlay

          // wrapper's centering.
          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.bag}"]`]: { display: 'flex' },

content.text:
Ground truth confirmed first: branch is `feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed` (matches task). Read `zimmProductCard/index.tsx`, `zimmProductCard.css.ts`, `zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx` + its `.css.ts`, `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`, the full theme stack (`globalStyles.ts`, `theme/index.ts`, base SFCC theme, Chakra's own `Link` recipe/`CSSReset`/`ChakraProvider` source in `node_modules`), `_app-config/index.tsx`, and the plan's own A2 section.

## Findings

**1. Focus-ring reset check — CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF, 🟡**

`MediaOnlyCardLink` (`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.tsx:611`, `<MediaOnlyCardLink to={href} display="block">` — no `sx`/`__css`/`className`) gets no theme styling at all: `zimmProductCard.css.ts` has zero `outline:` declarations anywhere (confirmed by grep, no hits).

No global outline reset exists in this codebase's own theme layer — `globalStyles.ts:287`'s only bare `outline: 'none'` is scoped to the opt-in `.zimm-form-control` class, not this link. Chakra's *own* `<Link>` recipe (`node_modules/@chakra-ui/theme/dist/components/link.js`) does set `outline: 'none'` + `_focusVisible: { boxShadow: 'outline' }`, but only fires via `useStyleConfig('Link', props)`, called inside Chakra's actual `Link` component (`node_modules/@chakra-ui/layout/dist/link.js`) — `chakra(RouteLink)` never calls that hook, so this recipe never applies here, exactly as assumed. `ChakraProvider`'s `resetCSS` defaults `true` (`node_modules/@chakra-ui/provider/dist/chakra-provider.js:37,58`) and `_app-config/index.tsx:210` doesn't override it, so Chakra's `CSSReset` is mounted; its one outline rule is polyfill-gated (`[data-js-focus-visible] :focus:not([data-focus-visible-added])...`), and `_app-config/index.tsx:17` imports the `focus-visible` polyfill globally — which marks genuine keyboard-Tab focus with `data-focus-visible-added`, explicitly excluded from that suppression rule. **So a real Tab keypress keeps the browser's native default outline — it is not stripped.** WCAG 2.4.7 is technically satisfied by the UA default; this is not a "no indicator at all" bug.

However, this codebase has an explicit, repeated, *written* convention against ever leaving an overlaid-on-a-photo control at just the bare default. `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts:163-165` and `:224-226` — the direct sibling molecule `MediaOnlyCardLink` wraps — state, verbatim, twice: *"Same uniform ring every other interactive control in ui-kits/ uses (...) — this overlay sits on top of a photographic image with only the bare browser-default outline otherwise."* `MediaOnlyCardLink` is now exactly that scenario (a link — the whole card, not just a small button — sitting on the photo) with no ring applied. A repo-wide grep for `outline`/`_focusVisible` across `overrides/` found every other interactive control (zimmColourSwatch, zimmNavItem, zimmColourSwatchGroup, zimmSizeChip, zimmSearchInput, zimmButton, zimmProductCardContent's nameLink/bagButton/notifyMeButton, zimmProductCardMedia's close/arrowButton, footer's links) carrying an explicit `var(--zimm-focus-ring)`-family rule. `MediaOnlyCardLink` is the only one with none.

**2. Recipe state exhaustiveness — vacuous, confirmed clean**

Per `plan.md`'s own citations and `index.tsx`'s docblock (lines 43-67), `recentlyViewed`'s Figma nodes (Desktop `40000307:12444` / Tablet `40000730:13363` / Mobile `40000538:25030`) are three static per-viewport instances — the plan's own rewritten note describes them as "a title row and five bare images, nothing else." Unlike home/plp/wishlist in the same docblock, which each cite an explicit `Default` **and** `Hover` node pair, no Hover/Active/Disabled node is ever cited for `recentlyViewed`. There is no designed state on record to cross-reference against the recipe, so this angle is vacuous here — the recipe correctly has zero entries for this element's states. (The absence of a *focus* spec specifically isn't unique to this variation either — `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts:18-22` notes no Figma focus spec exists anywhere in this family — so that overlap doesn't make this angle non-vacuous; the actionable gap is #1's, not #2's.)

**3. Hover-gating correctness — vacuous for the Link itself (confirmed); real secondary observation on the carousel**

Re-read `index.tsx:611-629`: `MediaOnlyCardLink` is `display="block"`, unconditional, no hidden/revealed state, nothing in the recipe targets it that way. Correctly not a hover-gated reveal — nothing to flag.

Bonus, CONFIRMED via re-reading `zimmProductCard.css.ts`'s docblock point 6 and its `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]` carousel block: the arrow reveal is scoped purely to `[data-card-slot="carousel"]` under the shared `root`, with **no** `data-card-slot="content"` requirement and **no** variation gate — the docblock says outright it's "unconditional... whenever a card has more than one image," and `styles.root` applies to the outer `chakra.div` in both branches. So if a caller ever passes >1 image to a `recentlyViewed` card (the same type-permitted scenario behind the already-confirmed double-fire click bug), hovering/focusing the card would visually reveal the arrows through this shared machinery inside the new `<Link>` — the styling half of the same gap, not a new independent defect. 🔵 informational, doesn't change the already-logged bug's status.

**4. Cross-check against `ProductNameLink` — CONFIRMED: this is a NEW gap, not a pre-existing pattern**

`zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx:39` — `const ProductNameLink = chakra(RouteLink);` — the identical factory pattern. Rendered at `index.tsx:210` with `__css={styles.nameLink}`; `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts:119-126`'s `nameLink` part carries `_focusVisible: FOCUS_VISIBLE`, where `FOCUS_VISIBLE` (lines 23-26) = `{ outline: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)', outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)' }`. So `ProductNameLink` does **not** rely on the browser default — its own file explicitly documents why: *"no Figma spec exists for focus on any of this component's three interactive parts (...) — this gap was caught twice already in this build (Step 2, Step 4); not repeating it"* (lines 18-22).

`MediaOnlyCardLink`'s own comment (`index.tsx:10-14`) says it copies "the same `chakra(RouteLink)` wrap `ZimmProductCardContent`'s own `ProductNameLink` already uses" — it copied the wrap, not the accompanying focus styling. So `MediaOnlyCardLink`'s reliance on the default is **new to A2**, not something A2 is merely consistent with — its own stated model does the opposite. This is functionally a third instance of the exact class of oversight the sibling file's comment says was already caught (and fixed) twice.

## Severity/status summary
| # | Status | Severity | Uniform/One-off |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | CONFIRMED | 🟡 | ONE-OFF |
| 2 | CONFIRMED vacuous | — | n/a |
| 3 | CONFIRMED vacuous (Link) + CONFIRMED secondary note (carousel) | 🔵 | n/a |
| 4 | CONFIRMED | 🟡 (sharpens #1) | ONE-OFF |

## Could not verify
- No way to render this in a real browser — can't see the actual visual focus ring (UA/OS-dependent styling for the unstyled default), only that source-level nothing strips it for a genuine keyboard Tab.
- Repo-wide `outline`/`_focusVisible` grep is a proxy, not exhaustive file-by-file coverage — a control styling focus some other way (no literal `outline`/`_focusVisible` token) wouldn't surface; spot-read files all matched consistently, so no positive reason to suspect a miss, but can't claim 100%.
- No independent Figma access for #2 (as stated up front) — conclusion is only as reliable as `plan.md`'s own node citations.
- Did not run any Vitest/Storybook file this session — judged unnecessary since every question here resolves from reading shipped source, not runtime behaviour.
